instrument: JV-043, Petition to Seal Juvenile Case Records, under 15 M.R.S. 3308-C(10)(A), printed Rev.12/21. This is sealing, not destruction or firearm-rights restoration.
filingActor: Person with the juvenile adjudication petitions and signs the Juvenile signature line. Official guidance permits assistance/request by parent, guardian or legal custodian; that does not authorize putting a helper's name in the juvenile's signature field or transferring participant ownership. Resolve actual representative authority when needed.
destination: The Juvenile Court holding the adjudication, within the Maine District Court, using the actual court town and docket. No statewide administrative mailing address is substituted for the case court.
trigger: Adjudication that would be murder, Class A/B/C, or OUI under 29-A M.R.S.2411 if adult; at least three years since discharge from the disposition; no juvenile adjudication or criminal conviction since the disposition date; no current adjudicatory proceedings for juvenile or other crime. Highest-class rules for mixed/multiple adjudications must be applied from the actual orders, not from a generic age-of-majority assumption.
timingDeadline: Three-year eligibility clock starts at discharge from the ordered disposition, while the clean-record condition runs from disposition. Section3308-C(10)(A) states no terminal petition filing deadline. The five-business-day automatic sealing rule belongs to (10)(C), not this petition. Do not promise an appeal deadline from this source review; a denial requires prompt legal assistance to determine and preserve the actual deadline.
requiredComponents: JV-043 identifying the juvenile, court town, docket, DOB, participant-provided gender and contact information, with genuine participant signature/date
Copy of the petition for the prosecuting attorney's office
Actual adjudication/disposition/discharge and intervening-history facts sufficient to verify the statutory conditions; the form itself does not provide separate boxes proving every condition
Any fact-specific supporting material requested by the court; no universal supporting affidavit, proposed order or notarization requirement established by the inspected form or subsection
feesWaivers: No current petition fee or exact waiver requirement was established from the inspected statute, blank or juvenile guide. Do not infer free filing from silence or reuse an adult-record-sealing price. Resolve any actual filing charge/waiver with the clerk of the selected juvenile case court; this local pricing input does not undo source recovery.
noticeService: JV-043 expressly requires a copy to the prosecuting attorney's office. No specific mail/personal-service deadline or mandatory certificate was established in the inspected sources; record real delivery and comply with the selected court's instructions without fabricating service. Subsection10(E) separately requires notice of a granting order to SBI when it maintains the juvenile history, followed by prompt record updating; do not conflate that post-order duty with petition service.
exactSelfHelpStop: Stop before filing when the petition-versus-automatic cohort, discharge date, intervening record, pending proceedings or representative authority is unresolved. Escalate a contested privacy/public-interest showing, opposition, hearing requiring advocacy, or denial to legal help while preserving actual deadlines. This is a proposed product boundary, not a statutory counsel mandate or new licensed-counsel adoption.
newResearch: Current official PDF text agrees with recovered blank identity, Rev.12/21, nonpublic marking and prosecutor-copy instruction. No fresh issuer-byte digest comparison was possible; old upload dates are not revision evidence.

The official court guide's no-appeal sentence conflicts with the current legislature text. 3308-C(10)(B) expressly gives a right to appeal denial under chapter509. Do not copy the guide's no-appeal claim into the packet; preserve prompt referral on denial.
The statutory petition and automatic branches remain separate. A form's silence on the three-year/history prerequisites is not permission to omit them from screening and instructions.
